automations.name: Verdict gate: a qa-tester SHIP verdict advances a programmer ticket out of Review

actions.author: automation
actions.content:
GIGACLAW-GATE v1 ticket-{ticketId} advanced — qa-tester returned SHIP.

The automation engine re-read the reviewer's `GIGACLAW-VERDICT v1` comment and re-checked it against the v1 contract (marker/body agreement, schema, no veto item on a SHIP) before moving this ticket to Done. Nothing was taken on the reviewer's word.

Artifact freshness is deliberately not re-hashed for qa-tester: its judgement covers a multi-file code change and an executed test run, not one workspace file, so no path evidence can hash to `inputDigest`. See `.agents/scripts/verdict.schema.json`.

automations.name: Verdict gate: a ticket stranded in Review on a spent reviewer-retry budget is blocked

actions.author: automation
actions.content:
GIGACLAW-GATE v1 ticket-{ticketId} blocked — stranded in Review with no usable verdict and no retry left.

The reviewer-retry budget for this episode is spent (a `GIGACLAW-REREVIEW v1` receipt on this ticket says the reviewer was already asked again), the newest verdict still resolves to `INVALID`, `STALE` or `MISSING`, and the ticket has been sitting in Review anyway.

Every other arm of the gate keys off a *new* reviewer comment. This one polls the column instead, so a ticket whose next comment never arrives — the reviewer crashed, or its re-dispatch never ran — terminates here rather than sitting in Review forever.

@owner — this ticket is now assigned to you. Read the newest reviewer comment, then either repair the reviewer's protocol and re-run it, or judge the work by hand. Check a candidate comment with `python3 .agents/scripts/verdict_contract.py --extract <comment-file> --out verdict.json`.
